title: Effects of generative artificial intelligence on instructional design outcomes and the mediating role of pre-service teachers' prior knowledge of different types of instructional design tasks
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the emerging question of how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support teachers in instructional design, particularly lesson planning, and whether teachers’ prior knowledge about instructional design tasks changes the way they benefit from GenAI. The authors frame the study around concerns that default chatbots such as ChatGPT may be useful for generating ideas and structures, but may also be insufficiently systematic and require critical user judgment. They also note that little research had examined the quality of GenAI-produced instructional design outcomes or the role of prior instructional design expertise.

The paper describes an experimental research proposal rather than completed results. It plans to compare four conditions: using GenAI directly, using a GPT bot pre-trained as a co-instructional designer, using an automated GPT-based generator, and a no-GenAI control group. Participants are pre-service teachers from Flemish university colleges and universities, and they will design a lesson blueprint and lesson plan for a two-hour history lesson. The study also plans to replicate the task across two instructional design contexts: lesson personalization and 4C/ID-based lesson design.

The proposed evaluation combines expert comparative judgment of the produced lesson designs with qualitative analysis of chatbot interactions. The study is grounded in prior knowledge theory, instructional design models, and chatbot design principles. Because the paper is a proposal/pilot-oriented description of a future study, it does not report empirical findings; instead, it argues that the research is needed to determine whether GenAI can serve as a useful co-design partner for teachers and under what conditions it improves instructional design quality.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based generative AI chatbot used for conversational text generation and assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by pre-service teachers to design a lesson blueprint and lesson plan under one experimental condition; also compared against a GPT bot pre-trained as a co-instructional designer and an automated GenAI condition.

quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a research proposal / experimental design paper and does not report results from a completed empirical study. It outlines planned conditions, measures, and analysis, but provides no outcome data.
impact_tier_rationale: No empirical effects are reported yet, so there is no demonstrated impact on instructional design quality or teacher practice in this paper.
